text:
nate: kicking off canary for release r-2026.03 on embeddings-service, shifting 10% traffic now. deploy-bot: canary shift started -> r-2026.03 @ 10% :rocket:

deploy-bot: traffic shift log: 
```
Shift: 0 -> 10%
Targets: embeddings-prod (eu-west, us-west)
Version: r-2026.03
Time: 2024-03-02T15:15:00Z
```

amy: ack. watching slo dashboard: https://grafana.company/redwood/embeddings-slo (p95 latency + error rate) :eyes:

amy: seeing a small bump in 5xxs in eu-west right after shift, from 0.2% -> 1.4% (last 5m)

liam: grabbing logs from the canary pods now, running `kubectl logs -l release=r-2026.03 -n prod --since=10m`

liam: I see a handful of `502 upstream read error` in the canary's nginx proxy, timestamps align with the traffic shift. Sample: `embed-worker: upstream read timed out while reading response header from upstream`

sarah: p95 latency also crept from 180ms -> 420ms for sequences >512 tokens. not huge but correlated.

nate: thanks. tagging the release notes: https://github.com/redwood/release-notes/blob/main/r-2026.03.md — includes a quantization/kvcache tweak.

amy: suggestion: pause ramp until we confirm root cause. we should hold at 10% for 30m and monitor. if 5xx > 1% sustained for 10m, consider rollback/pin. :warning:

deploy-bot: canary pause enforced by @nate (`policy: hold_on_error`)

deploy-bot: canary state -> PAUSED at 10% by nate at 15:19:04Z

liam: correlating with autoscaler churn — some canary pods restarted 2x during the shift. `kubelet: container runtime: out of memory` in one node (node-az3-gpu-12).

eva: that node had an older kernel patch? ops ticket  #OPS-1142 shows a kernelOOM backoff last week. might be unrelated but worth flagging.

nate: ok, two parallel workstreams: 1) investigate why canary nginx returned upstream read errors (liam + amy), 2) check node stability and pod memory footprints (eva + infra). Keep the hold.

sarah: I recommend pinning routing for the critical route `embeddings/vector` to previous stable version `r-2026.02` in case consumer apps depend on sub-1% error SLAs. We can do per-route pinning.

nate: good call. can we apply a per-route pin quickly? deploy-bot: run route pin `rbctl pin --route embeddings/vector --version r-2026.02 --reason "canary 5xx spike eu-west"`

deploy-bot: route pin applied -> embeddings/vector pinned to r-2026.02 by nate at 15:24:30Z :white_check_mark:

amy: after pin, external error rate for embeddings vector dropped back to 0.25% in the last 3m. internal canary still shows the spike (as expected).

liam: summary of logs: upstream timeouts originate from embed-worker v2 when processing long sequences. root cause hypothesis: a path in the new kvcache quantization that defers padding may cause a blocking syscall on certain token lengths. reproducing locally now.

eva: infra note: the OOMs were for transformer-batch-worker pods co-located on the same node. we've flagged node pool az3-gpu for cordon and reprovisioning to avoid noisy neighbor affecting canaries.

nate: decision: keep canary paused at 10%, route pinned to r-2026.02 for production traffic. no full rollout. escalate to release owner to decide next steps (hotfix vs revert). leave release notes draft open for update. -> owner: @sarah

sarah: acknowledged. I'll coordinate with research for a quick patch (kvcache early-exit) or revert the change. ETA initial assessment 60m. I'll post a final call here.

deploy-bot: action items logged: IH:1145 (investigate upstream timeouts), INFRA:1146 (az3-gpu reprovision), RELEASE:1147 (pin+hold summary).

amy: adding a quick smoke monitor: `monitoring alert` if embeddings route 5xx > 0.8% for 10m across any region.

nate: thanks everyone. keep updates short here. tag me for rollback decision. :thumbsup:

sarah: update @ 16:10Z — research reproduced the blocking path in local repro. preparing a minimal patch. if tests pass, we can patch and try a new canary later today. will also add a defensive timeout to the proxy.

nate: copying status to the oncall channel and release board. leaving canary paused until new canary validated. end thread. :lock:
